# Roblox Launch Kit

Goal: a launch that gets the game in front of the right players and keeps them, without hitting a publishing wall on launch day. On Roblox, distribution is earned: Recommended for You ranks games only by how organically arriving players engage (play through rate, first-session bounce, play days, playtime, co-play, spend), so the store page, the first three minutes and the reasons to return matter more than the ad budget.

Answer in the user's language; store copy in the languages the game targets (English first unless told otherwise).

Read `references/launch.md` every time: it holds the current platform rules (checked October 2026) and changes often.

## 1. Inputs
Take what is known from the conversation, `PRODUCTION_PLAN.md`, an idea-validator report or the game itself. Ask once with AskUserQuestion (multiple choice, recommended option first) only what is missing:
- State: not public yet / soft-launched / live and stagnating (then ask for the numbers: DAU, D1/D7 retention, average session, play through rate, Home Recommendation trend).
- Target audience: all ages (needs the Kids/Select evaluation) or 16+; owner: personal account or group; creator age and verification status.
- Launch date and whether it is fixed (event, creator collab, school holidays).
- Ad budget (none / small test / real campaign) and currency (card or Robux ad credits).

## 2. Readiness gate (blockers first)
Go through and mark each item done / missing / not needed:
1. **Publishing requirements** for the target audience (references section 1). For all ages: verification, 2FA, fee or 2 months of Plus/Premium, and the evaluation (trial with age-checked 16+ players until 250 unique plays by highly engaged age-checked users in 60 days). A fixed-date kids launch needs either that traffic beforehand or the 50,000 Robux expedited review: say this early, it changes the plan.
2. **Questionnaire** completed and accurate for every category.
3. **Game health**: run or offer `roblox-security-perf-audit` (exploits, backdoors, data loss, phone performance); purchases tested; Studio API access and product IDs set.
4. **First session**: playable within seconds of joining, the core loop understood in the first minute, a first reward before 60 s and a goal for the next session before 3 minutes (bounce rate is measured at < 60 s and 61-180 s). Phone controls and UI checked.
5. **Reasons to return**: daily reward or streak, next-goal UI, friends' progress, an upcoming event or update; easy co-play (invite prompts, party join, private servers).
6. **Analytics**: onboarding funnel (one step per tutorial step), shop funnel, economy events for every currency change, custom events for the core loop. Without them launch data is lost.
7. **Prices**: every Robux price in UI read from MarketplaceService (Managed Pricing changes prices per region); Dynamic Price Check done. `roblox-security-perf-audit`'s scanner flags hard-coded prices (`PRICE-HARDCODED`).

## 3. Store page
Write and check, in this order:
- **Name**: short, distinctive, says the genre or hook; no repeated words, no giveaway/Robux bait, at most one or two emojis; don't rename after launch without a reason.
- **Description**: hook in the first 160 characters (name + genre + unique feature + objective), then a short update blurb, the core loop and selling points, devices, codes, a tiny FAQ; under 1,000 characters; no hashtags or control lists.
- **Icon brief**: one subject, the game's main color, readable at 150 px and 64 px, no small text; plus 2 alternatives for later tests.
- **Thumbnail briefs** (3-5 for personalization): each sells a different reason to play (core action, social moment, progression/reward, event/update); real gameplay framed with free camera; nothing important in the bottom 15%; 1920x1080, under 3 MB.
- **Video** (optional): 15-30 s of real gameplay, rules in references section 3.

Then run the checker on the actual files (folder layout: `icon.png`, `thumbnails/*`, `title.txt`, `description.txt`):
```
python3 scripts/check_store_assets.py <store-dir> --preview store-preview.html
```
Fix every ERROR (upload rules) and every WARN unless there's a reason to keep it. Look at the preview (icon at 150/64 px on light and dark, thumbnails as Home tiles with the metadata overlay, the hook as mobile shows it); take a screenshot (Playwright or a headless browser) and actually look at it. If image-generation tools are connected, offer to mock thumbnails from real screenshots, but final images must show real gameplay.

## 4. Launch plan
Write `LAUNCH_KIT.md` in the project (ask before overwriting):

```
# <Game>: launch kit
Status, audience, launch date, budget, owner account

## Readiness gate
| Item | Status | Owner | Notes |

## Store page
Name, description (final text), icon and thumbnail briefs, checker result

## Pricing
| Item | Type (pass/product/subscription) | Price | Why this price | Dynamic price in UI |

## Measurement
Funnels and events, the 5 numbers to watch daily (PTR, first-play bounce, D1, D7, playtime per user), Home Recommendations benchmark comparison

## Traffic plan
Week 0 (private/friends test), soft launch, ad tests, community (group, Discord/YouTube/TikTok links), creators

## Ads
| Campaign | Objective | Audience | Budget/day | Days | Creatives | Success metric |

## 30-day live-ops calendar
| Week | Update / event | Goal metric | Store changes (thumbnails, event page) | Notifications |

## Risks
```

Rules for the plan:
- **Soft launch first**: limited audience or a small Plays campaign to measure PTR, bounce and D1 before spending more. Fix onboarding before scaling ads.
- **Ads**: start with Plays, small daily budget, 3-5 thumbnails per campaign, run several days before judging; Engagement objective only to reach the Kids/Select threshold (watch the Audience Reach dashboard and pause when reached). Ads help the game get considered; they don't count toward ranking, so retention decides what happens after.
- **Experiments**: one variable at a time (onboarding, starter pack, shop placement), 14+ days, one variant vs control.
- **Live-ops**: an update every 1-2 weeks with one goal metric each, events published as Experience Events (Trending Events needs 1,000+ RSVPs), update announcements to opted-in players, experience notifications for personal moments, new thumbnails tested with each major update. Plan around Saturdays and holidays.
- **Price optimization** only becomes available with roughly 60,000 transactions in 30 days; until then pick prices from comparable games and test with Experiments.

## 5. Already live and stagnating
Diagnose before prescribing: Analytics > Acquisition > Home Recommendations. Impressions fell after PTR fell -> icon/thumbnails/name; after bounce rose -> first session; after D2-7/D8-28 play days fell -> mid-term goals and content; benchmarks show which signal is furthest behind. Check the Creator Dashboard for a reduced-exposure quality banner (non-unique metadata or place, giveaway bait, mismatch). Then propose the 3 changes with the biggest expected effect and how to measure each.

## 6. Report
- Readiness verdict (ready / ready with risks / blocked by X) and the blockers with owners.
- Final store text, checker summary and preview path.
- The launch plan file and the first 3 actions for this week.
- What needs a human: verification, 2FA, paying the fee, uploading assets, the questionnaire, ad payment.

## Hand-off
`roblox-security-perf-audit` before going public; `roblox-ui-designer` for shop/onboarding UI fixes; `roblox-luau-codegen` for analytics events, dynamic prices, daily rewards, invite prompts and notifications; `roblox-game-idea-validator` if the numbers say the core loop itself doesn't hold players.

## File: references/launch.md

# Launch reference

Platform facts for publishing, discovery, pricing, ads and live-ops. Checked against create.roblox.com (Roblox/creator-docs) on 9 October 2026; Roblox changes these often, so re-check anything a launch date depends on. Items marked (verify) were not confirmed in that check.

## Contents
1. Who can play: audiences and publishing requirements
2. Maturity & Compliance Questionnaire
3. Store page: name, description, icon, thumbnails, video
4. How discovery works
5. Monetization and Managed Pricing
6. Analytics and experiments
7. Ads Manager
8. Events, update announcements, notifications
9. Earning programs

## 1. Who can play
Accounts are split by age (self-declared until age-checked):

| Account | Ages | Content it can see | Chat |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Roblox Kids | 5-8 | Minimal, Mild | off by default; parent can enable after age check |
| Roblox Select | 9-15 (or self-declared 9+ until checked) | Minimal, Mild, Moderate | off for self-declared; gradual with safeguards once checked |
| Roblox | age-checked 16+ | all rated content except Restricted (18+) | on by default where available |

**Reach 16+ (and Trusted Friends):** account in good standing and at least 2 days old, age verification (facial age estimation or government ID), Maturity & Compliance Questionnaire completed.

**Reach all ages (Kids and Select too):** all of the above plus
- account verification: facial age estimation if under 18, government ID if 18+; group games: the group owner;
- 2-step verification on the account;
- one of: an active Roblox Plus or Premium subscription for 2 consecutive months, OR the refundable publishing fee of 1,000 Robux per game (refunded when the game keeps 25 highly engaged players for 60 days without moderation; not refunded if the game is permanently moderated);
- evaluation: the game first runs as a trial for age-checked 16+ users; Roblox checks engagement is real (account age, play history, platform spend) and reviews safety; the game becomes eligible after **250 unique plays by highly engaged age-checked users within 60 days**. Progress: Creator Hub > Audience Reach dashboard.
- A "highly engaged player" currently needs account tenure, playtime in your game, and a purchase anywhere on Roblox in the last 60 days (not necessarily in your game).
- **Expedited review**: one-time refundable 50,000 Robux per game for timed launches or off-platform campaigns; refundable after 90 days if the game is in good standing with 25 highly engaged players.

Other publishing facts: up to 5 never-public private games can be made public per day; "Private" now means only editors can play; to let testers in, set Audience to Limited > Playtesters (requires meeting the public requirements). Public games can opt out of Recommended For You ("Exclude from Recommendations").

Launch implication: a brand-new game starts with 16+ age-checked players only. Plan the first weeks (ads, community, friends) to reach the 250 highly engaged plays, or budget the expedited fee for a fixed-date launch aimed at kids.

## 2. Maturity & Compliance Questionnaire
Answer accurately and update it when content changes. Categories: violence, blood, fear, crude humor, unplayable gambling content, strong language, romantic themes, alcohol, social hangout, free-form user creation, sensitive issues, paid random items, paid item trading, media, AI interaction. Labels: Minimal, Mild, Moderate, Restricted (18+ ID-verified only; the creator must be 18+ and verified). Unrated games lose reach. Source: production/promotion/content-maturity.

## 3. Store page
**Name**: keep it stable (renames lose search), no repeated words ("Obby Madness OBBY OBBY" gets demoted), at most one or two well-placed emojis. No official length limit is documented; short names read best on tiles.

**Description** (experimental guidelines, production/publishing/descriptions):
- 1,000-character budget.
- Hook = first ~160 characters: title, core genre, the most unique feature, primary search terms, the main objective. It is what search snippets and the collapsed mobile description show.
- Optional short "recent update" blurb; main content = core loop and selling points (bullets or a paragraph); additional info = devices, codes, short FAQ, link to a DevForum changelog.
- No tags/hashtags (unused by ranking), no control lists (teach them in game), all-ages wording.

**Icon** (production/publishing/experience-icons): square, 512x512 (at least); it is shown down to 150x150 and smaller, so preview it small. One icon per locale; must pass moderation. Express theme/tone/genre; unique and relevant imagery, strong color and contrast.

**Thumbnails** (production/publishing/thumbnails):
- Up to 10 images/videos on the detail page; images 16:9, ideally 1920x1080 (other ratios get stretched to 16:9); .jpg .gif .png .tga .bmp; Home page uploads under 3 MB.
- Don't put essential text or elements at the bottom: metadata like the player count can cover it.
- Thumbnail personalization (Home page tab): activate 2-5 thumbnails; Roblox shows each to random users, then gives more impressions to the winner per user group while still exploring. Measured by **qualified play through rate** (qualified plays / Home impressions). Reported average +8.5% qualified PTR, up to +50%. Keep several active; test new ones with each major update, then leave them until the next.
- Video: authentic gameplay only; free camera (Left Shift + P in a solo playtest), light color grading, logo overlay, Roblox catalog music are fine; no voice-over, narration or music with lyrics, no real-world footage, no ads/claims ("50% off", "Free UGC!"), no mechanics or graphics the game doesn't have. 3 video uploads per month (rejections count). Not shown on Xbox, PlayStation, VR.

**Other**: genre, supported devices, social links (production/promotion/social-media-links), localized name/description/icon for big languages (production/localization), badges for milestones (production/publishing/badges).

## 4. How discovery works (discovery.md)
Recommended for You works in two stages: **retrieval** (which games are considered for a user; helped by ads, curation, search, charts, friends, notifications, social sharing, even a small number of players) and **ranking** (how far it goes: ONLY the engagement of users who arrived organically from Recommended for You counts; ad, search, friend and social traffic do not count here).

Signals, averaged per user (small games are not disadvantaged):
- Most important: play through rate (plays after seeing it in Recommended for You); first play bounce rate (negative; < 60 s and 61-180 s sessions); play days per user and playtime per user (D1, D2-7, D8-28; playtime capped at 60 min per user per day).
- Important: intentional co-play days (friends joining, invites, private servers), qualified play sessions per user, spend days per user, Robux spent per user.
- Explore and expand: after an update Roblox may test the game on new cohorts; if they engage, it widens distribution.
- Weekly seasonality (peaks Saturday), summer/school, holidays.

What limits exposure: metadata leading with giveaways or Robux ("Robux! Play now!"), metadata that doesn't match gameplay, non-unique games (titles, images or place files close to existing games, also makes ads spend nothing). A banner on the Creator Dashboard shows quality issues; content quality is reassessed with every update.

Launch implications: the first 60-180 seconds decide the bounce signal (instant action, no long loading or menus); give a reason to come back tomorrow and in week 2-4 (play days); make playing with friends easy (co-play days); monitor Analytics > Acquisition > Home Recommendations against the benchmark games.

Other surfaces: Search (semantic, natural-language queries in supported languages), Discover charts and Trending, Standout Games (hand-curated), Live Events, Sponsored, game details page (events, groups, passes, similar games), notifications.

## 5. Monetization and Managed Pricing
- **Managed Pricing** (Monetization > Managed Pricing) = regional pricing + price optimization under one opt-in. New games and newly created items are enrolled by default; passes have regional pricing on by default; subscriptions, private servers and developer servers are regionalized automatically.
- Regional prices stay between 30% and 100% of your default price; economic location uses signals like VPN usage, billing and account history.
- Developer products need **dynamically scripted prices** before enabling: read `MarketplaceService:GetProductInfo(id, Enum.InfoType.Product)` (passes: `Enum.InfoType.GamePasses`) and show `PriceInRobux`; hard-coded UI prices show the wrong number while the player is charged the regional price. Use the Dynamic Price Check tool (up to 5 test accounts; "price pinned" or "location pinned") to find hard-coded prices.
- Protect gifts and trades between players with different price levels with `MarketplaceService:GetUsersPriceLevelsAsync`.
- Price optimization tests need roughly 60,000 transactions in the previous 30 days; a test runs about 3 weeks, applies new prices only if total revenue goes up, and repeats at least every 90 days.
- Product design: passes for permanent perks, developer products for repeatable items, subscriptions for recurring value, a free path for every core feature, contextual purchase prompts at natural moments (production/game-design/contextual-purchases, monetization-foundations).
- Paid random items: disclose in the questionnaire, show odds, check PolicyService per player.

## 6. Analytics and experiments
- Built-in dashboards: acquisition (incl. Home Recommendations tab with benchmark games), engagement, retention, monetization, performance, crashes, error reports, alerts, feedback, demographics.
- Custom events: economy events (every currency source/sink), funnel events (onboarding and shop; one step per tutorial step), custom events with custom fields. Plan them before launch so the first players' data isn't lost.
- **Experiments** (production/experiments): A/B tests on configs (in-game) or matchmaking; 14-60 days; up to two variants + control for in-game experiments; pick a goal metric, all metrics are tracked; watch the minimum detectable effect; prefer one variant vs control at 50/50 on a large rollout. Use for onboarding, shop visibility, starter packs, difficulty.

## 7. Ads Manager (production/promotion/ads-manager)
- Requirements: age 13+, verified email. Pay by card (18+, $1 temporary hold) or Robux converted to ad credits (13+, minimum 1 credit, irreversible). Group games supported (group ad account; "Configure and spend group revenue" permission for group funds).
- Objectives: **Plays** (most players likely to start a session; good for testing and to help recommendations learn), **Earnings** (limited availability; likely spenders), **Engagement** (age-checked highly engaged players who count toward the Kids and Select threshold; higher cost per play; doesn't auto-pause when the threshold is reached).
- Audiences: All, New (never played or 180+ days), Recent (played in 30 days; needs 10,000+ recent players), Lapsed (30-180 days; needs 20,000+ lapsed players); advanced targeting by location, age, gender, genre, device.
- Daily or lifetime budget, start date/time, duration; auto-reload for ad credits; payment method fixed after publishing. Up to 10 thumbnails per campaign (16:9, shown evenly), from Creator Hub, uploaded, or AI-generated. Campaigns show on Home (Sponsored) and in search. Moderation usually within 24 hours.
- Non-unique games can end with no spend and no conversions.
- Remember: ad players help retrieval but don't count in the ranking stage of Recommended for You. Use ads to test thumbnails/onboarding and to seed the first cohorts, not as a substitute for retention.
- Other promotion: share links and deeplinks, referral system, invite prompts, social media links, rewarded video ads (creator 13+ and ID-verified, public game with 2,000+ unique monthly visitors, reward must be a developer product; verify current terms), immersive ad placements (production/ad-placements).

## 8. Events, update announcements, notifications
- **Experience events** (Creator Dashboard > Engagement > Events & Updates): title, subtitle, description, category, start/end, place, public/private, event thumbnails (unique ones help; up to 5). Shown on the detail page (Join Event / Notify Me), on a shareable event page, on the group page. **Trending Events in Experiences** chart needs: active event started within the last 7 days, 1,000+ RSVPs, public.
- **Update announcements**: notify opted-in players of an update with a direct join link.
- **Experience notifications**: personalized notifications to opted-in users 13+ (milestones, friend activity, timers), sent from server scripts with the Open Cloud package from the Creator Store or via the Open Cloud UserNotification API; launch data readable with `Player:GetJoinData()`; in-game permission prompts to ask for opt-in. Notification strings are created in the Creator Dashboard.
- Cadence: weekly or bi-weekly updates with one measurable goal each; plan events around weekends (Saturday peak) and holidays; test new thumbnails with each major update.

## 9. Earning programs
- Creator Rewards (since 24 July 2025): Daily Engagement Rewards and Audience Expansion Rewards (see the production plan checklist); sessions over 10 minutes matter.
- Developer Exchange (DevEx) for cashing out; 18+ DevEx rate for Robux earned from 18+ purchases (production/monetization/18-plus-devex-rate) (verify current rates before quoting numbers).

# Roblox Luau Codegen

Goal: code that keeps working on a live server full of exploiters, phones and DataStore hiccups, not just in a Studio playtest, and that is structured so the team can keep building on it. The two things that destroy Roblox games after launch are lost/duplicated data and exploitable remotes, so those come from a tested template instead of being rewritten each time.

Answer in the user's language; write code, identifiers and code comments in English.

## 1. Inputs
- Look for `PRODUCTION_PLAN.md` / `tasks.csv` in the project (from the `roblox-game-production-plan` skill) and use its task IDs, data fields, products and analytics events. Without a plan, work from the conversation; for a single small script, skip the plan entirely.
- Scope: by default the scripting, data, monetization and analytics tasks of the current milestone (MVP first). State the task list you will implement in one line and continue; ask only if the scope is unclear.
- Delivery, ask once with AskUserQuestion if it is not obvious:
  1. **Rojo project on disk** (default when working in a folder or repo): files under `src/`, synced to Studio with Rojo.
  2. **Straight into Studio** when Roblox Studio MCP tools are connected: same hierarchy, created with the Studio tools (`list_roblox_studios` first, confirm the place).
  3. **Paste-ready**: every file with its exact Studio location and script type.

## 2. Scaffold (once per project)
Copy `assets/template/` into the project root. Never overwrite existing files; if the project already has its own structure, adapt the template modules into it instead of forcing the layout.

| File (Studio location) | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `default.project.json` | Rojo mapping below |
| `src/shared` -> ReplicatedStorage.Shared | `Config` (data defaults, product/pass IDs), `Net` (all remotes, validation, rate limits), `Guard` (validators) |
| `src/server/init.server.luau` -> ServerScriptService.Server (Script) | Boots every module in `Services`: `Init()` then `Start()` |
| `src/server/Services/DataService.luau` | Session-locked DataStore profiles, autosave, BindToClose, migrations, Studio mock |
| `src/server/Services/PurchaseService.luau` | Idempotent `ProcessReceipt`, pass ownership cache |
| `src/client/init.client.luau` -> StarterPlayerScripts.Client (LocalScript) | Boots every module in `Controllers` |
| `src/client/Controllers/DataController.luau` | Read-only synced copy of the player's data for UI |
| `selene.toml`, `stylua.toml` | Lint and format config |

Read the template files before extending them: their public functions are the contract every new system uses. The template and `references/patterns.md` were tested (session locking, purchases, remotes) and their Roblox API calls checked against current docs: don't "correct" them from memory. If something there looks wrong, keep it and raise it in the report. Then fill `Config.DefaultData` from the plan's data (currencies, inventory, progression, settings, timestamps) and put products/passes from the plan into `Config.Products` / `Config.Passes` with ID `0` and a `-- TODO: paste ID from Creator Hub` comment.

## 3. Write the systems
Read `references/patterns.md` before writing systems: it holds the coding rules, ready patterns (currency + analytics, shop, cooldowns, hit validation, rounds, placement, NPC pathfinding, leaderboards, codes, daily rewards, text filtering, PolicyService, animations, UI controllers) and the security checklist.

- Server logic: `src/server/Services/<Name>Service.luau`; client: `src/client/Controllers/<Name>Controller.luau`; shared tuning/item tables: `src/shared/<Name>Data.luau`. Modules expose `Init()` (no yielding; only set up own state or register with another service, e.g. `PurchaseService.RegisterProduct`) and `Start()` (connect events, start loops, use other services).
- Start each module with a short header: which plan tasks it implements (`-- Plan: SYS-03, SYS-04`) and its public API.
- Remotes: add the name to `Net.Events` / `Net.Functions`, handle on the server with `Net.handle` / `Net.handleInvoke` and `Guard` validators for every argument; the client only sends intents (`Net.fire("BuyItem", itemId)`), never results.
- Persistent state only through `DataService.Update`; new fields go into `Config.DefaultData`; renames or type changes get a migration and a `Config.Data.Version` bump.
- Developer products: `PurchaseService.RegisterProduct` in a `MonetizationService`; pass perks through `PurchaseService.OwnsPass` and `OnPassPurchased`.
- Analytics events from the plan: economy events after every successful currency change, funnel steps for onboarding and shop.

## File: references/patterns.md

# Roblox Luau patterns

Rules and patterns for systems built on the template (`DataService`, `PurchaseService`, `Net`, `Guard`, `Config`). Snippets assume the usual service locals (`local Players = game:GetService("Players")`, etc.) and the template modules required at the top.

## Contents
1. Coding rules
2. Security checklist
3. Patterns: currency + analytics, shop, cooldowns, hit validation, round state, interactions, placement, NPC pathfinding, leaderboards, codes, daily rewards, text filtering, PolicyService, animations, sounds, UI controllers, monetization service

## 1. Coding rules
- `game:GetService` for every service; `task.wait/spawn/delay/defer` (never `wait`, `spawn`, `delay`); `os.clock()` for durations, `os.time()` for saved timestamps.
- Set properties first and `Parent` last on new instances; don't use the `Instance.new(class, parent)` form.
- Modern APIs: `Animator:LoadAnimation` (not `Humanoid:LoadAnimation`), `LinearVelocity`/`AlignPosition`/`AlignOrientation` (not `BodyVelocity`/`BodyPosition`/`BodyGyro`), `workspace:Raycast` + `RaycastParams`, `GetPartBoundsInBox`/`GetPartsInPart` + `OverlapParams`, `UserInputService`/`ContextActionService` (not `Mouse`), `TextChatService`.
- Handle players already in game and characters already spawned: loop `Players:GetPlayers()` after connecting `PlayerAdded`; check `player.Character` before `CharacterAdded`.
- Clean up per-player and per-character state on `PlayerRemoving` and `Humanoid.Died`/`CharacterRemoving` (tables keyed by Player leak otherwise). Disconnect connections you own.
- Client code assumes streaming: `WaitForChild(name, timeout)` and nil checks for anything in Workspace.
- Asset IDs (animations, sounds, images) live in one shared module (e.g. `src/shared/Assets.luau`), not scattered literals.
- Performance: no per-part `while true` loops; one loop or `RunService.Heartbeat` handler per system iterating a set built with `CollectionService` tags; visuals (tweens, particles, camera) on the client; server only does authority.
- Type annotations on public functions; add `--!strict` when the team uses luau-lsp.

## 2. Security checklist
The client is controlled by the player. For every remote and every system ask:
- Does the server decide the outcome (currency, damage, price, ownership, cooldown, position, timer)? The client only says what it wants.
- Every argument validated with `Guard` (type, range, length, membership, Instance class and ancestry). NaN and huge numbers rejected (Guard.number does this).
- Is the player allowed to do this now: alive, in the right round/state, owns the item/plot, close enough, off cooldown?
- Rate limited (Net default 10/s; lower for expensive or economy actions).
- Instances passed by the client are re-checked: still exist, belong to this player or are public, within range.
- No remote that runs arbitrary code, sets arbitrary properties or accepts paths.
- NPCs and server-owned physics: `PrimaryPart:SetNetworkOwner(nil)`.
- Data: changes go through `DataService.Update`; never trust a client copy; purchases only through `PurchaseService`.
- Player text is filtered before anyone else sees it.

## 3. Patterns

### Currency change + analytics
Signature (checked against create.roblox.com, Oct 2026): `LogEconomyEvent(player, flowType, currencyType, amount, endingBalance, transactionType, itemSku?, customFields?)`. Amount comes before the balance.
```lua
local AnalyticsService = game:GetService("AnalyticsService")

local CurrencyService = {}

function CurrencyService.Add(player: Player, amount: number, transactionType: string, sku: string): boolean
	local changed = DataService.Update(player, function(data)
		data.Coins += amount
	end)
	if changed then
		local data = DataService.Get(player)
		AnalyticsService:LogEconomyEvent(
			player,
			Enum.AnalyticsEconomyFlowType.Source,
			"Coins", -- currencyType
			amount, -- amount of this transaction (always positive)
			data.Coins, -- endingBalance after it
			transactionType, -- e.g. Enum.AnalyticsEconomyTransactionType.Gameplay.Name
			sku -- itemSku
		)
	end
	return changed
end

-- Returns false (and changes nothing) if the player can't afford it.
function CurrencyService.Spend(player: Player, amount: number, transactionType: string, sku: string): boolean
	local spent = false
	DataService.Update(player, function(data)
		if data.Coins >= amount then
			data.Coins -= amount
			spent = true
		end
	end)
	if spent then
		local data = DataService.Get(player)
		AnalyticsService:LogEconomyEvent(
			player,
			Enum.AnalyticsEconomyFlowType.Sink,
			"Coins", -- currencyType
			amount, -- amount (positive, the dashboard shows sinks as negative)
			data.Coins, -- endingBalance
			transactionType,
			sku
		)
	end
	return spent
end
```

### Shop (in-game currency)
Prices live in a shared table the server enforces; the client only names the item.
```lua
-- src/shared/ItemData.luau
local ItemData = {
	Items = {
		Sword = { Price = 100 },
		Bow = { Price = 250 },
	},
	Ids = {} :: { string },
}
for id in ItemData.Items do
	table.insert(ItemData.Ids, id)
end
return ItemData
```
```lua
-- ShopService.Start()
Net.handle("BuyItem", { Guard.oneOf(ItemData.Ids) }, function(player, itemId)
	local data = DataService.Get(player)
	if not data or data.Inventory[itemId] then
		return
	end
	local price = ItemData.Items[itemId].Price
	if CurrencyService.Spend(player, price, Enum.AnalyticsEconomyTransactionType.Shop.Name, itemId) then
		DataService.Update(player, function(playerData)
			playerData.Inventory[itemId] = true
		end)
	end
end, { rate = 2 })
```

### Server cooldowns
```lua
local lastUse: { [Player]: { [string]: number } } = {}

local function tryUse(player: Player, ability: string, cooldown: number): boolean
	local uses = lastUse[player]
	if not uses then
		uses = {}
		lastUse[player] = uses
	end
	local now = os.clock()
	if uses[ability] and now - uses[ability] < cooldown then
		return false
	end
	uses[ability] = now
	return true
end

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
	lastUse[player] = nil
end)
```

### Hit validation (melee)
The client may play the swing and report a target; the server checks everything and computes damage.
```lua
local RANGE = 8
local TOLERANCE = 4 -- latency slack

Net.handle("Attack", { Guard.instance("Model", workspace) }, function(player, target)
	local character = player.Character
	local root = character and character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	local humanoid = character and character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	local targetRoot = target:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	local targetHumanoid = target:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	if not (root and humanoid and targetRoot and targetHumanoid) then
		return
	end
	if humanoid.Health <= 0 or targetHumanoid.Health <= 0 or target == character then
		return
	end
	if (root.Position - targetRoot.Position).Magnitude > RANGE + TOLERANCE then
		return
	end
	if not tryUse(player, "Attack", 0.5) then
		return
	end
	targetHumanoid:TakeDamage(10)
end, { rate = 5 })
```
Projectiles: the server either simulates them or checks that the origin is near the character and the direction is plausible, then raycasts itself.

### Round / game state
Broadcast state with attributes (they replicate) instead of extra remotes.
```lua
local STATES = { "Intermission", "Day", "Night", "Results" }
local DURATIONS = { Intermission = 15, Day = 120, Night = 90, Results = 10 }

local function setState(state: string, endsAt: number)
	workspace:SetAttribute("GameState", state)
	workspace:SetAttribute("StateEndsAt", endsAt) -- client shows a countdown from workspace:GetServerTimeNow()
end

task.spawn(function()
	while true do
		for _, state in STATES do
			local duration = DURATIONS[state]
			setState(state, workspace:GetServerTimeNow() + duration)
			task.wait(duration)
		end
	end
end)

-- Client: workspace:GetAttributeChangedSignal("GameState"):Connect(updateUi)
```

### Interactions
`ProximityPrompt.Triggered` fires on the server with the player and the engine already checks distance; still check game rules.
```lua
local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")

local function setupStation(station: Instance)
	local prompt = station:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("ProximityPrompt", true)
	if not prompt then
		return
	end
	prompt.Triggered:Connect(function(player)
		if workspace:GetAttribute("GameState") ~= "Day" then
			return
		end
		-- server-side effect here
	end)
end

CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal("Station"):Connect(setupStation)
for _, station in CollectionService:GetTagged("Station") do
	setupStation(station)
end
```

### Placement (building, towers, furniture)
The client previews and sends the item and a desired position; the server snaps, checks ownership/bounds/overlap/cost and builds the real object.
```lua
local GRID = 4

Net.handle("Place", { Guard.oneOf(ItemData.Ids), Guard.vector3(10000) }, function(player, itemId, position)
	local plot = getPlot(player) -- the player's own area (Part); returns nil if none
	if not plot then
		return
	end
	local snapped = Vector3.new(
		math.round(position.X / GRID) * GRID,
		plot.Position.Y + plot.Size.Y / 2,
		math.round(position.Z / GRID) * GRID
	)
	local localPos = plot.CFrame:PointToObjectSpace(snapped)
	if math.abs(localPos.X) > plot.Size.X / 2 or math.abs(localPos.Z) > plot.Size.Z / 2 then
		return
	end
	local params = OverlapParams.new()
	params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Include
	params.FilterDescendantsInstances = { plot.Placed }
	local size = Vector3.new(GRID - 0.1, 4, GRID - 0.1)
	if #workspace:GetPartBoundsInBox(CFrame.new(snapped + Vector3.new(0, 2, 0)), size, params) > 0 then
		return
	end
	local price = ItemData.Items[itemId].Price
	if not CurrencyService.Spend(player, price, Enum.AnalyticsEconomyTransactionType.Gameplay.Name, itemId) then
		return
	end
	-- clone the model from ServerStorage, PivotTo(CFrame.new(snapped)), parent to plot.Placed, save to data if persistent
end, { rate = 4 })
```

### NPC pathfinding
```lua
local PathfindingService = game:GetService("PathfindingService")

local function walkTo(npc: Model, goal: Vector3): boolean
	local humanoid = npc:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	local root = npc.PrimaryPart
	if not humanoid or not root then
		return false
	end
	root:SetNetworkOwner(nil)
	local path = PathfindingService:CreatePath({ AgentRadius = 2, AgentHeight = 5, AgentCanJump = true })
	local ok = pcall(path.ComputeAsync, path, root.Position, goal)
	if not ok or path.Status ~= Enum.PathStatus.Success then
		return false
	end
	local blocked = false
	local connection = path.Blocked:Connect(function()
		blocked = true
	end)
	for _, waypoint in path:GetWaypoints() do
		if blocked or humanoid.Health <= 0 then
			break
		end
		if waypoint.Action == Enum.PathWaypointAction.Jump then
			humanoid.Jump = true
		end
		humanoid:MoveTo(waypoint.Position)
		if not humanoid.MoveToFinished:Wait() then
			break -- MoveTo timed out (stuck)
		end
	end
	connection:Disconnect()
	return not blocked
end
```
Re-call `walkTo` when it returns false. Many NPCs: stagger path computations, reuse paths for groups, use simple `MoveTo` on open ground.

### Leaderboard (OrderedDataStore)
```lua
local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local board = DataStoreService:GetOrderedDataStore("Coins_v1")

local function submit(player: Player, value: number) -- on leave and every few minutes, not every change
	pcall(board.SetAsync, board, tostring(player.UserId), math.floor(value))
end

local function top(count: number): { { key: string, value: number } }
	local ok, pages = pcall(board.GetSortedAsync, board, false, count)
	if not ok then
		return {}
	end
	return pages:GetCurrentPage()
end
-- Refresh the shown board every 60-120 seconds; resolve names with Players:GetNameFromUserIdAsync (cache it).
```

### Codes
```lua
local CODES = {
	LAUNCH = { Coins = 500, Expires = os.time({ year = 2027, month = 1, day = 1, hour = 0 }) },
}

Net.handleInvoke("RedeemCode", { Guard.string(32) }, function(player, input)
	local code = string.upper(input)
	local reward = CODES[code]
	if not reward or os.time() > reward.Expires then
		return "Invalid"
	end
	local granted = false
	DataService.Update(player, function(data)
		data.RedeemedCodes = data.RedeemedCodes or {}
		if not data.RedeemedCodes[code] then
			data.RedeemedCodes[code] = true
			data.Coins += reward.Coins
			granted = true
		end
	end)
	return if granted then "Redeemed" else "AlreadyUsed"
end, { rate = 1, burst = 3 })
```
Add `RedeemedCodes = {}` to `Config.DefaultData` instead of the inline fallback when writing it for real.

### Daily reward
```lua
local DAY = 24 * 60 * 60

local function claimDaily(player: Player): boolean
	local claimed = false
	DataService.Update(player, function(data)
		local now = os.time()
		if now - (data.LastDaily or 0) >= DAY then
			data.Streak = if now - (data.LastDaily or 0) < 2 * DAY then (data.Streak or 0) + 1 else 1
			data.LastDaily = now
			data.Coins += 50 * math.min(data.Streak, 7)
			claimed = true
		end
	end)
	return claimed
end
```

### Filtering player text
```lua
local TextService = game:GetService("TextService")

local function filterForEveryone(player: Player, text: string): string?
	local ok, result = pcall(TextService.FilterStringAsync, TextService, text, player.UserId)
	if not ok then
		return nil -- don't show unfiltered text
	end
	local okText, filtered = pcall(result.GetNonChatStringForBroadcastAsync, result)
	return if okText then filtered else nil
end
```

### PolicyService (paid random items, trading)
```lua
local PolicyService = game:GetService("PolicyService")

local function canBuyRandomItems(player: Player): boolean
	local ok, policy = pcall(PolicyService.GetPolicyInfoForPlayerAsync, PolicyService, player)
	return ok and not policy.ArePaidRandomItemsRestricted
end
-- Same pattern: policy.IsPaidItemTradingAllowed before enabling Robux-bought item trading.
```

### Animations
Upload animations to the account or group that owns the experience and give the experience permission, otherwise they play in Studio and fail for players. Load once per character, play many times.
```lua
local Assets = require(ReplicatedStorage.Shared.Assets) -- { Animations = { Chop = "rbxassetid://..." } }

local function loadTracks(character: Model): { [string]: AnimationTrack }
	local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid") :: Humanoid
	local animator = humanoid:WaitForChild("Animator") :: Animator
	local tracks = {}
	for name, id in Assets.Animations do
		local animation = Instance.new("Animation")
		animation.AnimationId = id
		local track = animator:LoadAnimation(animation)
		track.Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action
		tracks[name] = track
	end
	return tracks
end
```
Play the local player's animations on the client (they replicate); play NPC animations on the server. Use `track:GetMarkerReachedSignal("Hit")` for timing instead of `task.wait`.

### Sounds
UI and feedback sounds on the client (`SoundService:PlayLocalSound(sound)`); 3D world sounds parented to a part; every `Sound` in a `SoundGroup` (Music, SFX, UI) whose `Volume` the settings menu controls.

### UI controller
Layout is built in StarterGui by the UI designer; the controller binds to it by name, reads `DataController`, sends intents with `Net`.
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local DataController = require(script.Parent.DataController)
local Net = require(ReplicatedStorage.Shared.Net)

local HudController = {}

function HudController.Start()
	local gui = Players.LocalPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui"):WaitForChild("Hud")
	local coinsLabel = gui:WaitForChild("Coins") :: TextLabel
	DataController.OnChanged(function(data)
		coinsLabel.Text = tostring(data.Coins)
	end)
	local buyButton = gui:WaitForChild("BuySword") :: TextButton
	buyButton.Activated:Connect(function()
		Net.fire("BuyItem", "Sword")
	end)
end

return HudController
```
Use `Activated` (works for touch, mouse and gamepad), Scale-based sizes, and test in the device emulator.

### Monetization service
```lua
local MonetizationService = {}

function MonetizationService.Init()
	PurchaseService.RegisterProduct(Config.Products.Coins500, function(_player, data)
		data.Coins += 500
	end)
end

function MonetizationService.Start()
	local function applyPerks(player: Player)
		if PurchaseService.OwnsPass(player, Config.Passes.VIP) then
			player:SetAttribute("VIP", true) -- read by other systems (e.g. 2x coins), replicated to UI
		end
	end
	Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(applyPerks)
	for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
		task.spawn(applyPerks, player)
	end
	PurchaseService.OnPassPurchased(function(player, passId)
		if passId == Config.Passes.VIP then
			player:SetAttribute("VIP", true)
		end
	end)
end

return MonetizationService
```
Calling `RegisterProduct` in `Init` is fine: it only fills a table.

## Files not included here

Scripts and assets of this skill. Download them from https://github.com/G3LO1/gelo/tree/main/plugins/roblox-studio/skills/roblox-luau-codegen (paths relative to that folder):

- `assets/template/default.project.json`
- `assets/template/selene.toml`
- `assets/template/src/client/Controllers/DataController.luau`
- `assets/template/src/client/init.client.luau`
- `assets/template/src/server/Services/DataService.luau`
- `assets/template/src/server/Services/PurchaseService.luau`
- `assets/template/src/server/init.server.luau`
- `assets/template/src/shared/Config.luau`
- `assets/template/src/shared/Guard.luau`
- `assets/template/src/shared/Net.luau`
- `assets/template/stylua.toml`
- `scripts/check.sh`

# Skill: roblox-map-builder

**When to use:** Build aesthetic, accurate and performant Roblox Studio maps (terrain, buildings, lighting, props, procedural generation, validation) in any style: low-poly, cartoon, realistic, horror, neon/sci-fi, fantasy, retro, PS1, cozy town. Use for any Roblox map, level, biome, lighting or 'mapa w robloxie' request.

Skill folder (scripts, assets): https://github.com/G3LO1/gelo/tree/main/plugins/roblox-studio/skills/roblox-map-builder

## File: SKILL.md

# Roblox Map Builder

Goal: maps that look good AND are correct (scale, collision, navigation, performance). Process beats presets: greybox first, style second, validate always. All numbers below are starting points to playtest, not Roblox standards.

## Workflow
1. Brief: gameplay, camera + avatar, target device (phone?), STYLE, area size, landmark, time of day, existing assets/palette. Ask every decision with AskUserQuestion (multiple choice, recommended option first) rather than free text; ask only what is missing. If style unclear, propose 2-3.
2. Greybox with plain Parts on ONE grid; one landmark per zone; routes spawn -> goals; check scale vs avatar. Screenshot + playtest before detailing.
3. Terrain pass (outdoor): macro shape -> routes -> biome blending (irregular bands) -> cliffs/caves -> water. Parts/meshes for collision-critical edges.
4. Kit + dressing: modular pieces with shared mesh/texture IDs, palette + material rules from the style, asymmetric prop clusters, story-driven wear. Hierarchy: big shapes -> medium rhythm -> small detail.
5. Lighting pass LAST: apply style preset, tune against screenshots. Never use fog/bloom to hide geometry problems.
6. Validate (checklist below), fix, re-check, then report briefly: what was built, what was verified, what needs a human (real phone test, uploads, manual Studio toggles).

## Studio loop
With Roblox Studio tools (execute_luau, multi_edit, insert_asset, screen_capture, start_stop_play, get_console_output, inspect_instance, search_game_tree, generate_mesh/material/texture): build -> screen_capture from player height -> playtest -> read console -> revise. Always list_roblox_studios first and confirm the target place before modifying. Inspect before editing; small reversible edits; put output under Workspace/Map/{Architecture,TerrainDetails,Props,Gameplay,Spawns}; store Seed as an attribute on Map; never touch existing user scripts without saying so.

## Custom meshes with Blender
When the style needs meshes the Studio tools can't make well (modular kit pieces, stylized trees/rocks, props), check for a connected Blender MCP server (tools with `blender` in the name; ToolSearch `blender`). If there is none, ask once whether the user has Blender and offer to connect it (`../roblox-animation-vfx/references/blender.md` section 1), or continue with parts, terrain, generate_mesh and Creator Store assets. With Blender: Roblox units and axes, pieces on the map grid with consistent pivots, <= 20,000 triangles, one material per mesh, shared textures; run `../roblox-animation-vfx/scripts/blender_check.py` (mode model) through the code tool, export, import piece by piece (3D Importer: Upload to Roblox with the owner as Creator, Insert Using Scene Position), assemble in Studio.

## Hard rules
- Use Lighting.LightingStyle (Realistic|Soft) + PrioritizeLightingQuality; Lighting.Technology is deprecated (Future=Realistic+prioritized, ShadowMap=Soft+prioritized, Voxel=Soft+not prioritized). VERIFIED: LightingStyle is script-writable via execute_luau in Edit mode.
- Atmosphere overrides legacy FogStart/FogEnd. Neon does not light anything (add Point/Surface/SpotLight). ShadowSoftness is Realistic-only. ClockTime never advances without a script. Shadows vanish below graphics level 4.
- Terrain color: Terrain:SetMaterialColor() (per material, global). Terrain.Decoration (grass blades), GrassLength (0.1-1), StreamingEnabled are Studio-side and NOT scriptable: for low-poly/cartoon tell the user to untick Decoration in Properties. MaterialVariant on terrain = global override of the base material. Terrain voxels are 4x4x4 studs.
- Place templates ship with Bloom/DepthOfField/SunRays: when applying a preset delete or merge them so template and custom effects don't stack.
- No universal part/light-count limit: budget the visible scene on a baseline device; measure (Shift+F2 render stats, F9 memory, Ctrl+Alt+F6 MicroProfiler). Illustrative only: <1000 draw calls, <1M visible tris; imported mesh max 20,000 tris.
- Procedural generation must be seeded (Random.new(seed+n), math.noise), constrained (slope, spacing, path/landmark reservations) and validated (connectivity, spawn safety, pathfinding).
- Don't recreate specific copyrighted maps/assets; use lessons only. Inspect Toolbox models for scripts and scale.

## Core numbers
- 1 stud ~ 0.28 m. Classic avatar ~5 studs, humanoid 6-6.5. Jump height default 7.2. Door ~3-3.4 x 7.3-7.7 (realistic) or 5-7 x 8-10 (game-scale); ceiling 8.6-9.6 real / 10-14 game; stair rise 0.5-1 run 2-3; lane 10.7-12.9. Pick realistic OR enlarged circulation, never mix.
- One kit grid before placing (4 or 8 residential, 16 ship/station, 32 Backrooms). Consistent lower-corner pivots. No coplanar overlapping faces. Anchor static geometry.
- Streaming start: Improved / PauseOutsideLoadedArea / MinRadius 64 / TargetRadius 1024 / Opportunistic; static chunks Model.LevelOfDetail=SLIM, modules <= ~64 studs/dim.
- Collision by role: floors/walls CanCollide true; decor CanCollide/CanTouch/CanQuery false; CollisionFidelity Box->Hull->Default->Precise (cost order); simple invisible colliders on key walkways.
- Pathfinding defaults AgentRadius 2, AgentHeight 5, WaypointSpacing 4: set for the real NPC, check Path.Status spawn->goal, recompute on Path.Blocked.
- Textures: 1024^2 = 4x memory of 512^2; <=512 for most, <256 minor. MaterialVariant = tileable PBR, SurfaceAppearance = UV mesh. Reuse asset IDs. Particles ceiling 400/s (100/s mobile), budget far lower.

## Learned in practice (low-poly island ~200x200, verified in Studio)
- Island on Terrain: delete Baseplate, FillBlock in 4-stud columns; height = radial falloff + big Gaussian hill + 2 octaves math.noise; irregular coast radius via noise on angle; materials by height/slope: Sand beach, Rock steep, Grass top, Ground along the path.
- Water: ocean ring strips PLUS a Sand seabed underneath, else hard seam at the coast.
- Faceted canopy: MANY small/medium rotated cubes in an ellipsoid, 3-4 green shades, lowest mass below the widest point. One huge cube = blocky; thin stack = lollipop. Trunk = crossed blocks + root buttresses, pivot at base, bury 0.5-1 stud.
- Scatter: raycast Terrain, Grass only, Normal.Y >= ~0.78-0.86, min spacing ~8, exclude path/landmark/spawn, grove centers. First pass is usually too sparse: do a denser second pass. Target ~75 trees / 26 rocks / 19 bushes per 200x200.
- Spawn: search the flattest spot (minimise height spread across pad corners), re-screenshot to confirm it sits flush.
- Screenshots: use player-height cameras outside canopy blocks.
- Final checks that worked: 0 unanchored parts, Pathfinding Success spawn->goal, playtest with clean console.

## Style cheat-sheet (starting presets)
LOW-POLY: SmoothPlastic, 4-6 related swatches + 1 accent, S 30-70% V 55-90%. Soft or Realistic (Realistic = sharper facets); CT 14, B 2, Ambient #697A83, OutdoorAmbient #A9C5C5, ShadowSoftness 0.35; Bloom 0.08/20/1.5; Atmosphere Density 0.12 Haze 0.2; SunRays 0.05/0.25. Faceted silhouettes decided before modeling; trees 5-8 sided trunk + angular canopy masses, 14-25 studs; one unmistakable landmark.
CARTOON/TYCOON/OBBY: Soft; CT 14, B 2.5, Ambient #9AA6B6, OutdoorAmbient #C8DDF0; Sat +0.08; Bloom 0.12/24/1.6; Atmosphere Density 0.08. One ground hue + one architecture hue + one action hue, S 45-85% V 70-95%; max saturation only for rewards/hazards/signs. Chunky bevels 0.5-2 studs; exact-edge gameplay in parts not terrain.
REALISTIC: Realistic + PrioritizeLightingQuality; CT 14, B 2.2, Exposure -0.1, ShadowSoftness 0.35, Env diffuse/specular scale 1, Ambient (55,58,62), OutdoorAmbient (118,125,132); Atmosphere Density 0.22 Haze 0.8 Color (195,210,225); Contrast 0.04 Sat -0.04; Bloom 0.12/18/1.8. PBR albedo without baked shadows, OpenGL normals, asphalt non-metallic; grid 4/8; scatter foliage in groves via raycast; no live mirror reflections. Fake-realism order of failure: scale -> silhouettes -> materials/sky -> lighting support -> noisy decals -> effects.
HORROR/BACKROOMS: Realistic; CT 0, B 1.4, Ambient (58,53,40), OutdoorAmbient (65,61,47); Atmosphere Density 0.12 Haze 0.6 Color (196,184,135); Contrast 0.04 Sat -0.12; Bloom 0.12/18/1.2. Route readable without flashlight (next decision visible 12-25 studs); 32x32 module kit; ceiling SurfaceLight 1-2 / Range 12-18 / no shadows; rare flicker on ONE fixture, reduced-flash option; positional audio (RollOff 6-35); seeded DFS room generator with door-mask templates (bits N1 E2 S4 W8) guarantees reachability only, not pacing.
NEON/CYBERPUNK/SCI-FI: Realistic; CT 0.5-2, B 1-2, Ambient #1A2030, OutdoorAmbient #30304A; Atmosphere Density 0.2-0.35 Haze 0.5-1.5; Bloom 0.2-0.45 / 20-36 / 0.85-0.95; Contrast 0.05-0.15. ~75% dark / 20% mid / 5% accent (cyan #23E5F3, magenta #F046C7, violet #865BFF, amber #FFB347). Neon only on thin strokes + real lights beside it; wet roads via roughness 0.15-0.3 puddles, metalness ~0; SurfaceGui signs LightInfluence 0, AlwaysOnTop false; street 20-32, buildings 48-160, 16-stud ship kit.
FANTASY/NATURE: layout hub -> roads -> biome entrances -> dungeon/castle; sizes: path 8-12, road 16-24, cottage 16-24 wide walls 9-12, doorway 5-7 x 8-10, wall 4-8 thick x 18-30, tower 14-24 dia x 28-50, dungeon module 16 or 32. Cobblestone/WoodPlanks/Slate/Brick. 5-12 big trees per 100x100 patch in groves, no grids; irregular biome seams via pass/river/ridge. Golden-hour: CT 17, B 2, OutdoorAmbient (145,125,105), Atmosphere Color (215,188,145) Density 0.28 Haze 1.2. Tropical CT 13 Atmosphere (183,224,212) 0.32/1.6. Snow CT 11 Sat -0.12. Desert CT 15 Haze 2.0 Sand (207,174,116). Post-apoc CT 16 B 1.3 Sat -0.35 Contrast 0.14. One Lighting per place: pick compatible baseline.
RETRO/CLASSIC: Soft, CT 14, B 1.5-2, flat grays Ambient ~(115-128), little/no bloom; Plastic/SmoothPlastic, anchored rectangular parts. BLOCKY/VOXEL: fixed 2- or 4-stud cube grid (terrain voxels are not crisp cubes). PS1: 64-256 px textures, SurfaceAppearance.ResampleMode=Pixelated, Soft, B 1, Exposure -0.2, Sat -0.18, light fog. CEL-SHADE: matte SmoothPlastic + baked 2-3 color bands, Highlight (FillTransparency 1, Occluded; limit 255) or inverted-hull outlines, don't outline everything. SPLATOON-TOON: neutral architecture + bold team colors, ink as bounded marks not unlimited decals. COZY TOWN: grid 4, bay 4/8 wide, story 9-11 high, door 5-6 x 8-9, lot 40x48..48x64, street 18-24 + 4-6 sidewalk, warm PointLight (255,210,160) Range 8-14, furnish interaction zones, Soft CT 17 B 2.

## Validation checklist (before done)
1 Scale: avatar fits all doors/corridors, jumps match CharacterJumpHeight. 2 Seams: no gaps/z-fighting/floating/buried props; static parts anchored. 3 Collision by role. 4 Spawns on stable flat ground, clear exits, away from hazards; test first spawn AND respawn. 5 PathfindingService route spawn->every goal (tag goals "Goal"), Status Success. 6 Readability in grayscale and with post-FX off; landmark visible from spawn. 7 Test Soft + low graphics, interiors and openings separately. 8 Performance via render stats/F9/MicroProfiler on densest vista, real phone if possible. 9 Scripts tolerate streaming. 10 Organized folders, names, CollectionService tags, seed stored as attribute. 11 Playtest with start_stop_play and read get_console_output: clean.

## Common failures
Flat empty expanses; detail everywhere; mixed styles; cloned trees on a grid; doors blocking NPCs; seams/z-fighting; bloom/fog masking; template + custom post-FX stacked; giant models, unique meshes, particle vistas; "fine in editor" but untested at avatar height, low graphics, phone.

# Skill: roblox-security-perf-audit

**When to use:** Audit an existing Roblox game for security holes and performance problems: exploitable remotes (client-sent prices/damage, missing validation and rate limits), Toolbox backdoors (require(id), getfenv, loadstring, webhooks, hidden code), data-loss and duplication risks (SetAsync, no session lock, multiple ProcessReceipt), hard-coded Robux prices that break Managed Pricing, and lag sources (loops without yields, per-frame allocations, unanchored parts, precise collisions, shadow lights, particle rates, NPC humanoids, no streaming). Runs a static Luau scanner and a place audit (in Studio or on .rbxl/.rbxm files), then gives a prioritized fix list and patches. Use whenever someone asks to check, audit, review or secure their Roblox game or scripts, mentions exploiters, hackers, backdoors, viruses in free models, data loss, duplication, lag, low FPS, memory or crashes on phones, or says 'sprawdź grę', 'czy mój kod jest bezpieczny', 'gra laguje', 'wirus w modelu'.

Skill folder (scripts, assets): https://github.com/G3LO1/gelo/tree/main/plugins/roblox-studio/skills/roblox-security-perf-audit

## File: SKILL.md

# Roblox Security & Performance Audit

Goal: find what will actually hurt the game in production (exploiters, backdoors, lost or duplicated data, lag on phones) and fix it in order of damage, with proof. Scanners find candidates fast; a human-style review of the remotes and a measurement on a real device decide what is real.

Answer in the user's language; rule IDs, code and identifiers stay in English.

## 1. Scope
Find out, from the conversation or with one AskUserQuestion round (multiple choice, recommended first), only what is missing:
- What to audit: code on disk (Rojo project), a place in Studio (Roblox Studio MCP connected), a `.rbxl/.rbxlx/.rbxm/.rbxmx` file, or a single script pasted in chat.
- The symptom, if any: exploiters doing X, data loss/duplication, lag (where, on which devices), memory crashes, a suspicious free model. A symptom narrows the audit; without one, run everything.
- Whether you may change code or only report. Default: report first, then patch what the user approves.

## 2. Run the scanners
Both are read-only and live in `scripts/`.

**Code** (any folder of `.lua/.luau`, or `.rbxmx/.rbxlx` files):
```
python3 scripts/scan_luau.py <src-or-files> [--json findings.json] [--fail-on high|medium|low|none]
```
22 rules (`SEC-*`, `DATA-*`, `PURCHASE-*`, `PRICE-*`, `PERF-*`); each finding has a severity, file:line, server/client context and the reason. Context comes from file names (`.server.luau`, `.client.luau`), folders (`server`, `ServerScriptService`, `client`, `StarterPlayer`...) or the script class in XML.

**Place** (instances, settings, and every script's source):
- In Studio with MCP: `list_roblox_studios`, confirm the place, then run the whole of `scripts/audit_studio.luau` with `execute_luau` (Edit mode is fine). It prints the report and returns it.
- On a file: `lune run scripts/audit_place.luau <file> [--dump-scripts <dir>] [--json report.json] [--fail-on ...]`. Use `--dump-scripts` and run `scan_luau.py` on the dump to scan binary places' code too. Rojo project: `rojo build -o place.rbxl` first. Lune can't read `CollisionFidelity` back from saved files; the report lists those meshes under `collisionFidelityUnreadable` (check them in Studio).
- No Studio, no file: ask the user to save the place (File > Save to File As) or to run `audit_studio.luau` in the Command Bar and paste the output.

The place audit checks: backdoor patterns in any script, scripts inside Workspace models, LoadStringEnabled, loose unanchored parts, precise collisions, tiny collidable decor, small shadow casters, semi-transparent overdraw, shadow-casting lights, particle rates (400/s cap, 100/s on phones) and total particle budget, lifetimes over the 20 s cap, NPC humanoid count, unique meshes, oversized models, streaming off on big maps, character cleanup, stacked post-processing.

Treat every finding as a lead: open the code or instance and confirm it before reporting it as a problem. Thresholds are in `Audit.Thresholds` at the top of `audit_studio.luau`; adjust them for the game (an NPC horde game expects more humanoids) and say so.

## 3. Review what scanners can't see
Read `references/security.md` and do at least:
1. **Remote inventory**: a table of every remote with its arguments, server checks, rate limit and verdict (OK / FIX / CRITICAL). CRITICAL = the client decides an outcome (currency, damage, rewards, ownership, other players' state).
2. **Trust boundaries**: movement and physics ownership for anything competitive, Touched handlers, admin commands (UserId on the server).
3. **Data and purchases**: session locking, BindToClose, one idempotent ProcessReceipt, prices from MarketplaceService.
4. **Toolbox and plugins**: for every model with scripts, read the scripts; for backdoors follow the clean-up steps (remove, search the whole place again, sandbox what stays, rotate keys).

For performance, read `references/performance.md`. If Studio is connected, playtest (`start_stop_play`) and read `get_console_output`; otherwise give the user the measurement steps (Developer Console memory, MicroProfiler on the densest view, Scene Analysis, a real low-end phone). Never claim the game runs well on phones without a measurement.

## 4. Fix
- Order: CRITICAL security and backdoors -> data loss/duplication -> purchases -> high performance issues (freezes, crashes) -> medium -> low.
- Patch with the smallest change that removes the cause; reuse the project's own validation layer. In projects built with `roblox-luau-codegen`, use `Net` schemas + `Guard` validators and `DataService.Update` instead of hand-rolled checks.
- Never delete or rewrite the user's scripts or models without saying exactly what and why and getting a yes; for Toolbox backdoors, show the offending lines first.
- After fixing, run the same scanners again and show the before/after counts; re-run the playtest when Studio is connected.

## 5. Report
1. Verdict in one line (e.g. "2 critical exploits, 1 backdoor, lag from 3 emitters; fixable in a day").
2. Findings table: severity, where (file:line or instance path), what goes wrong in production (one sentence a non-programmer understands), fix, status (fixed / proposed / needs a human).
3. Remote inventory table.
4. What was verified (scanners, playtest, device) and what was not.
5. Manual steps: Studio settings (LoadStringEnabled, HTTP, API access, third-party teleports/sales), sandboxing models, testing on a real phone, rotating keys after a backdoor.

## Hand-off
Offer `roblox-luau-codegen` to rebuild a broken system on the tested template (session-locked data, idempotent purchases, validated remotes), and `roblox-map-builder` to rebuild heavy map areas with a modular kit and streaming.

## File: references/performance.md

# Performance review

How to measure and what usually fixes it. Sources: create.roblox.com/docs/performance-optimization (identify, improve, design, scene analysis, test on hardware), checked October 2026. Budgets are starting points: measure on the weakest device you support, before and after each fix.

## Contents
1. Measure first
2. Script computation and memory
3. Physics
4. Humanoids and NPCs
5. Rendering
6. Networking
7. Assets, memory, load time
8. Phone checklist

## 1. Measure first
- **Developer Console** (F9, also in live servers): Log for errors/warnings, Memory (client and server: LuaHeap, InstanceCount, PlaceScriptMemory, graphics/texture, sounds, animation), Network, Scripts (activity per script).
- **MicroProfiler** (Ctrl+Alt+F6, or dump from the Dev Console on a phone): frame time spikes and which scopes take them. Server profiles can be captured from the Dev Console too.
- **Scene Analysis** (Window > Performance Summary > Scene Analysis, in a play session): script memory, unparented instances (held by scripts), instance composition, audio memory, animation memory, triangle and draw call composition.
- **Render stats** (Shift+F2) for draw calls and triangles; **Performance** dashboard in Creator Hub analytics for live FPS, memory, crash rate and join time by device.
- Test in the Device Emulator for layout, but performance only on real low-end phones (the documented recommendation).

Record a baseline: FPS and frame time on the densest view, client memory, server heartbeat, join time. Fix the biggest cost first, then measure again.

## 2. Script computation and memory
- Expensive work tied to frame events (`RenderStepped`/`PreRender`, `Heartbeat`, `Stepped`): move it to timers, event-driven updates or spread it across frames; never create instances or call `GetDescendants` every frame. `RenderStepped` blocks rendering: keep it for camera/character work only.
- Big table operations every tick: cache results, update incrementally.
- Leaks: connections never disconnected (the engine never collects a connected callback and what it references), tables of players/instances never cleaned on leave, instances removed from the tree but still referenced (Scene Analysis "unparented instances"), animations/sounds kept alive by scripts. Watch LuaHeap and InstanceCount over a long session: steady growth is a leak.
- `Workspace.PlayerCharacterDestroyBehavior = Enabled` destroys leavers' Player and character objects automatically.
- Parallel Luau (Actors) for heavy independent work (pathfinding batches, procedural generation, raycast fans).

## 3. Physics
- Anchor everything that doesn't need simulation.
- Adaptive physics stepping instead of a fixed high rate.
- Fewer, simpler mechanisms; fewer constraints per assembly.
- CollisionFidelity: Box or Hull for props, Default for most, PreciseConvexDecomposition only where exact collision matters. Decor: CanCollide, CanTouch and CanQuery off.
- Many loose parts settling (debris, ragdolls): clean them up, or make them client-only effects.

## 4. Humanoids and NPCs
- Disable HumanoidStateTypes NPCs never use (`Humanoid:SetStateEnabled`), especially Climbing, Swimming, FallingDown, Ragdoll, GettingUp, Flying, Seated where not needed.
- Static or scripted NPCs: AnimationController + Animator instead of a Humanoid.
- Play NPC animations on clients when there are many NPCs.
- Pool NPC models instead of destroying and cloning; spawn NPCs only near players.
- Don't change sizes/scales or rebuild the avatar hierarchy during gameplay (FastCluster rebuilds).

## 5. Rendering
- Draw calls matter more than triangles: reuse the same meshes and textures (instancing), avoid many unique meshes, decals, textures and particle emitters in one view. Property changes on ParticleEmitters are costly.
- Culling: streaming + `Model.LevelOfDetail = SLIM` for world models, `Workspace.EnableSLIMAvatars` for crowds; `MeshPart.RenderFidelity = Automatic` or `Performance`.
- Shadows: `CastShadow` off on small and distant parts, shadows on only a few local lights.
- Transparency overdraw: avoid stacks of semi-transparent parts, big particles, layered glass.
- Particles: up to 400/s per emitter (100/s on phones), lifetime capped at 20 s. Prefer few large particles or `Emit()` bursts over high rates; disable emitters out of view.
- Skinned MeshParts moving outside a Humanoid model and Models with too many parts both force FastCluster rebuilds.

## 6. Networking
- Remote traffic: send ids and deltas, not whole tables every frame; batch; use `UnreliableRemoteEvent` for frequent cosmetic updates that can be dropped.
- Server-side TweenService replicates every step: tween on clients, set the final value on the server.
- Creating or deleting big instance trees replicates all of it: build big maps in chunks, keep templates in ServerStorage, clone near players.
- Clean animation metadata from rigs; don't replicate what clients never need (keep server-only assets in ServerStorage).

## 7. Assets, memory, load time
- Upload each asset once and reuse its id (duplicates load twice); the 3D Importer doesn't de-duplicate meshes, so import kit pieces one by one.
- Texture memory depends on pixels, not file size: 1024x1024 costs 4x of 512x512. Most images <= 512, minor ones <= 256. Trim sheets for architecture.
- Audio: don't preload every track; load per area/state.
- Instance streaming (StreamingEnabled) for large maps: lower memory and faster joins; client code must handle parts that aren't streamed in yet (WaitForChild with timeouts, `Model.ModelStreamingMode`, `Player:RequestStreamAroundAsync`).
- Join time: keep ReplicatedFirst small (loading screen only), defer non-critical assets with ContentProvider:PreloadAsync on what the first screen needs.

## 8. Phone checklist
- [ ] 30+ FPS on the densest view on a low-end phone, no hitches when the core loop's effects play.
- [ ] Client memory stable over a 30-minute session.
- [ ] Join to playable under ~15-20 s on mobile data.
- [ ] Graphics quality 1-3 still readable (shadows and some effects vanish).
- [ ] No server heartbeat drops with a full server and the maximum number of NPCs/projectiles.

## File: references/security.md

# Security review

What to check by hand after the scanners. Sources: create.roblox.com/docs/scripting/security (client-server boundary, security tactics, third-party vulnerabilities, server-side detection), checked October 2026.

## Contents
1. Threat model
2. Remote inventory (do this for every game)
3. Validation checklist
4. Movement and physics
5. Backdoors and Toolbox assets
6. Data and purchases
7. Detection and consequences
8. Settings to check

## 1. Threat model
An exploiter fully controls their own client. They can:
- fire every RemoteEvent / invoke every RemoteFunction with any arguments, any types, at any rate, in any game state;
- read every LocalScript, ModuleScript and instance that replicates to them (ReplicatedStorage, ReplicatedFirst, their PlayerGui, Workspace), so "hidden" remotes and client-side secrets don't exist;
- change anything on their own client (UI, local values, cooldowns, other players' visuals) and anything they have network ownership of: their character (speed, teleport, fly, noclip) and unanchored parts the engine handed to them;
- delete LocalScripts, including client anti-cheats.

They cannot change server state directly. Every exploit is the server trusting something the client said or something the client simulates.

## 2. Remote inventory
List every remote (search `RemoteEvent`, `RemoteFunction`, `UnreliableRemoteEvent`, `FireServer`, `InvokeServer`, `OnServerEvent`, `OnServerInvoke`, and the project's own wrapper such as `Net.handle`). For each, fill one row:

| Remote | Direction | Arguments (type, range) | Server checks | Rate limit | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BuyItem | C -> S | itemId: string in Items | exists, price from server table, enough coins, not owned | 3/s | OK |
| DealDamage | C -> S | target: Model, damage: number | none | none | CRITICAL: client sets damage |

Verdicts: OK, FIX (missing check), CRITICAL (client decides an outcome: currency, damage, rewards, ownership, position of others). Remotes that only one side should use: server -> client remotes must have no `OnServerEvent` handler at all, and the server never calls `InvokeClient`.

## 3. Validation checklist
For every argument of every client -> server remote:
- **Type**: `typeof(x) == "string"` etc. Instances: `typeof(x) == "Instance"` and `x:IsA(...)`. Tables: check shape and size; reject unexpected keys.
- **Numbers**: reject NaN (`x ~= x`), +/-inf, non-integers where integers are expected (`x % 1 == 0`), negatives, out-of-range values. Clamp nothing silently that should be rejected.
- **Strings**: max length, allowed characters, `utf8.len` not nil; filter with TextService before anyone else sees it.
- **Identity and ownership**: the player argument is the only trusted identity. An item/plot/pet/vehicle id must belong to that player on the server.
- **Context**: game state allows it (round running, player alive, in the shop zone), distance from the player's character to the target (server positions, with tolerance for latency), line of sight if it matters.
- **Cooldown and rate**: per player, per remote; reject over the limit instead of queuing.
- **Outcome on the server**: prices, damage, rewards, drop tables, odds come from server-side tables keyed by an id the client sent.
- **RemoteFunctions**: the server must return quickly and never yield on client data; never `InvokeClient`.

The `roblox-luau-codegen` template does this through `Net` (declared schemas + per-remote rate limits) and `Guard` validators; patch new code to use them instead of hand-written checks.

## 4. Movement and physics
- Players always own their character's physics: speed, teleport and fly hacks are possible. Check on the server: distance moved per second (with generous tolerance for lag and legitimate boosts), position inside allowed areas, grounded time. Rubber-band to the last valid position rather than kicking.
- Unanchored parts near a player may be handed to that player's client. For anything gameplay-critical (ball, vehicle in a race, moving platform): `part:SetNetworkOwner(nil)` on the server, or anchor and move it with the server.
- Touched events fire for exploiters too, from any distance they can move a part to: re-check distance and state in the handler.

## 5. Backdoors and Toolbox assets
- Every Creator Store model can contain scripts. Toolbox shows when a model has scripts; inspect before inserting and prefer assets you or trusted creators made.
- Backdoor signs: `require(<number>)`, `getfenv`/`setfenv`, `loadstring`, long escaped strings or `string.char` chains, code pushed off-screen with whitespace, HTTP calls to webhooks or paste sites, scripts named like engine objects ("Weld", "Fire", "Script ") inside props, `InsertService:LoadAsset` of unknown ids, plugins that insert scripts.
- Sandboxing (Script Capabilities, beta): set `Workspace.SandboxedInstance` to `Experimental`, set the model's `Sandboxed` to true and grant only the `Capabilities` it needs. Never grant Network, DataStore, AssetRequire, CapabilityControl or LoadString to third-party assets unless you know exactly why.
- Plugins run with full Studio access: install only from creators you trust and remove unused ones.
- After removing a backdoor: search the whole place again (backdoors often copy themselves into several models), check ServerScriptService, ServerStorage, Lighting, ReplicatedFirst, StarterPack/StarterGui and Teams, rotate any Open Cloud API keys the place used.

## 6. Data and purchases
- Player data: session locking (UpdateAsync with a lock or a proven library), save on leave, BindToClose and autosave, schema version with migrations, every DataStore call in pcall with retries. `SetAsync` on player data is a red flag.
- `ProcessReceipt`: exactly one in the whole game, server-side, idempotent (store PurchaseIds), grants and saves before returning `PurchaseGranted`, returns `NotProcessedYet` when the player's data isn't loaded.
- Prices shown in UI come from `MarketplaceService:GetProductInfo(id, Enum.InfoType.Product / GamePass)` (`PriceInRobux`), because Managed Pricing (regional pricing + price optimization, on by default for passes) changes what each player pays. Hard-coded prices show the wrong number.
- Trades and gifts between players with different regional prices: gate them with `MarketplaceService:GetUsersPriceLevelsAsync` to prevent price arbitrage.
- Paid random items and trading: check PolicyService per player.

## 7. Detection and consequences
- The server decides. Client-side detections are only hints; never ban on them.
- Prevent harm first: drop the request, clamp, re-sync, rubber-band. Punish only to protect others.
- Heuristics as signals: rate of gain, completion time, action cadence. Add to a per-player suspicion score; act when several independent signals agree.
- Honeypot remotes: a remote no legitimate client ever fires; firing it is strong evidence.
- Consequence ladder: silent logging -> quiet mitigation -> temporary restrictions (trading, leaderboards) -> kick/temporary ban -> permanent ban. Delay visible consequences so exploiters can't tell what triggered them. For repeat offenders use the Ban API (`Players:BanAsync`) instead of kicks.
- Admin and moderator commands: check `UserId` (or group rank) on the server for every command, never names or a client flag.

## 8. Settings to check
- ServerScriptService.LoadStringEnabled: off.
- Game Settings > Security: Allow HTTP Requests only if the game uses HttpService; Enable Studio Access to API Services only in development places if testers shouldn't touch live data.
- Third-party teleports and Third-party sales: off unless needed.
- Team Create collaborators and group roles with edit access: only people who need it; 2FA on accounts that can publish.

## Files not included here

Scripts and assets of this skill. Download them from https://github.com/G3LO1/gelo/tree/main/plugins/roblox-studio/skills/roblox-security-perf-audit (paths relative to that folder):

- `scripts/audit_place.luau`
- `scripts/audit_studio.luau`
- `scripts/scan_luau.py`

# Skill: roblox-ui-designer

**When to use:** Design and build Roblox game UI (HUD, shop, inventory, menus, popups, loading screens) in Figma, Photoshop or straight in Roblox Studio: proposes fitting UI styles (bubbly cartoon, clean minimal, glass, anime/gacha, sci-fi neon, horror, pixel, cozy pastel, competitive HUD, fantasy, comic meme) with ready color/font/shape tokens, designs mobile-safe layouts, converts PSDs and Figma designs, and generates a validated build script (+ .rbxmx) that creates the ScreenGuis and a StyleSheet theme in Studio. Use whenever someone wants UI, GUI, HUD, menus, buttons, a UI style or theme for a Roblox game, or asks 'zrób UI', 'jaki styl UI', 'przenieś UI z Figmy/Photoshopa do Roblox'.
